solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant, where cropped, eaten by horse

indicators.note: eaten by means the cropped word goes inside the horse

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, so the final letter of where is lost

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that a plant somewhere has been nibbled down by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropped' trims a word by its end; 'eaten by' places the trimmed word inside the horse. 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowherb is a pink-flowered weed of the pink family, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Farm tea made special with carrot cake ingredient?

indicators.note: made special means made into something different, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A farmhouse tea becomes a treat with carrot cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made special' rearranges FARM TEA plus CARROT; the surface wants carrot cake as one item.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream of tartar is a raising agent used in baking, so an ingredient of cakes.

clue.text: Driver in West, a fellow doomed

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed or beyond help

explanation.surface: A cowboy driver in the Wild West is a doomed man.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner drives a horse-drawn wagon, so is a driver.

clue.text: Demand that performance is never to be put on again?

definitions.meaning: to insist on or require something

definitions.text: that performance is never to be put on again?
definitions.meaning: a former act, one that is now ex, never to be staged again

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a show must never be staged again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as EX-ACT, a performance that is a thing of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand or extract something, such as payment or obedience.

clue.text: Black reptile doubling up a bit in bad weather

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: doubling up a bit means one letter of the reptile is written twice

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile

explanation.surface: A dark reptile curls up in rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubling up a bit' doubles the Z of LIZARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with high winds, very bad weather.

clue.text: Left-winger is distraught, ultimately leaving party

indicators.note: leaving means the following letters depart from the left-winger's word

parts.note: a socialist is a political left-winger

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of distraught

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist storms out of a party, upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T from distraught; 'leaving' removes IS plus T (IST) from the end of SOCIALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering, a synonym for a party.

clue.text: Just under ten short soldiers turning up to register

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut

parts.note: nine is just under ten

explanation.surface: Nearly ten soldiers arrive at a camp to enrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns GIS to SIG; 'short' trims NINE to NIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign in is to record your arrival, a phrasal synonym for register.

clue.text: Positive guy with conceit, wealthy husband doing a bunk

parts.note: cat is slang for a guy or bloke
ego is self-regard or conceit

indicators.note: doing a bunk is British slang for running off, so the husband letter leaves

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A vain man is sure of himself, and his rich husband runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a bunk' (British slang for running away) takes H out of RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Categoric means absolute and unqualified, as in being positive or certain.

clue.text: Comic needing an act of reflection

parts.note: a and an are both the indefinite article
musing is the act of reflecting or pondering

explanation.surface: A comedian needs to perform a thoughtful routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link. 'Comic' reads as a noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic and amusing are synonyms, both meaning funny.

clue.text: Work of art futile ultimately — no good, mad

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of futile

parts.note: raving means mad, as in raving mad

explanation.surface: An art critic dismisses a work as pointless, worthless and deranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print made from a cut plate, an example of a work of art.

clue.text: Trips from this French city?

definitions.meaning: journeys or excursions taken for pleasure
the city on the Loire in central France

explanation.surface: A travel brochure advertises outings starting from a particular French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link: the word for trips is also the name of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tours means excursions, and Tours is a cathedral city on the river Loire.

clue.text: Having nothing to worry about, like a model in more ways than one?

definitions.text: like a model in more ways than one?
definitions.meaning: a model both sits for an artist and is pretty

explanation.surface: A carefree person is compared to a model, in several senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting pretty is an idiom for being in a comfortable, advantageous position.

clue.text: Artist paid to pen article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the article goes inside

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A painter is paid to write an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid' is the past of meet, as in meeting a bill; 'to pen' means to enclose rather than to write.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: I repeatedly get excited, with enthusiasm about current climate

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the mixed letters

parts.note: zest means keen enthusiasm

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
repeatedly means the letter I is used twice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting worked up and enthusiastic about the present climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the I, 'excited' signals the anagram, and 'about' wraps the enthusiasm word round the mixed letters; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeitgeist is German for spirit of the age, the prevailing mood or intellectual climate of the times.

clue.text: Woodman's line of business, needing fine minerals to test

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ores are mined minerals
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A woodsman's trade requires fine minerals for testing.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the management of woods and timber, the trade of a woodman.

clue.text: Period home with good taste is what I provide

parts.note: a season is a period of the year
in means at home

explanation.surface: A holiday home with good taste promises what it offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; the clue speaks as the answer, which gives food its flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoning such as salt and pepper adds flavour to food.

clue.text: Smile endlessly, repeatedly showing charm

indicators.note: repeatedly means the shortened word appears twice
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone keeps smiling without stopping, displaying charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts GRIN to GRI; 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grigri is an African amulet or talisman, a charm in the magical sense.

clue.text: College room without roof — thus useless for learner to enter

indicators.note: without roof in a down clue means the top letter goes

parts.note: a hall is a large room
so means thus

indicators.note: to enter means the learner letter goes inside

parts.note: US is short for unserviceable, so useless
L is the learner plate letter

explanation.surface: A college room with no ceiling is no use to a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without roof' drops the top letter in a down clue; 'to enter' puts the learner inside; 'for' is a link. US for useless is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls is a college of Oxford University with no undergraduates.

clue.text: Holiday month with endless rest for one imposing hard task on hero

definitions.text: one imposing hard task on hero

parts.note: Aug is short for August, the main summer holiday month

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A holiday month with unbroken rest, for someone who sets a hero a hard job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the last E from EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: King Augeas owned the filthy stables that Hercules had to clean as one of his twelve labours.

clue.text: Fool overwhelmed by heartless avarice must be brought down

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the fool goes inside
heartless means one of the middle letters is removed

parts.note: greed is avarice
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool consumed by greed will come to a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes one middle letter to leave GRED; 'overwhelmed by' puts the fool inside; 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass an opponent is to fell them, as in a tackle in sport.

clue.text: Indication of very bad bruising on member who is unpopular worker?

parts.note: badly bruised skin turns black, as in black and blue
a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: A dark bruise on a limb marks someone who is disliked at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackleg is a strikebreaker, a worker resented by colleagues on strike.

clue.text: Old English composer's measure of brightness

definitions.meaning: a unit of luminance in physics

explanation.surface: A historic English composer's yardstick of brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant Lambert wrote Rio Grande, and a lambert is an old unit of luminance.

clue.text: Classical artist irritated about onset of impressionism

indicators.note: about means the irritated phrase wraps round the letter

parts.note: got to someone means irritated them

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of impressionism

explanation.surface: An old master is annoyed by the rise of Impressionism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' gives I; 'about' puts GOT TO round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giotto was an early Italian painter, an artist of the classical tradition.

clue.text: Brewing is to cease — before these are brought out?

indicators.note: brewing means being stirred up or developing, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An instruction that brewing must stop before certain items are fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewing' rearranges IS TO CEASE; 'before' is a link. The surface steers towards tea itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea cosies are produced to keep the pot warm once tea is made.

clue.text: Performer with animal has monkey around not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the quiet letter is dropped

parts.note: to tamper is to meddle or monkey around
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A circus performer whose monkey fidgets about noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamer trains and performs with wild animals such as lions.

clue.text: Apprehending end of joke, you chuckle

indicators.note: apprehending means catching, so the old pronoun holds the letter

parts.note: thee is an old form of you

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of joke

explanation.surface: Getting the punchline, you laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives E; 'Apprehending' puts THEE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is a giggle or snigger, a type of chuckle.

clue.text: Sage in Nagpur — I shine

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wise man in the Indian city of Nagpur boasts of his brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu holy man or seer, a sage.

clue.text: Expression of pain by one in ordeal most bad-tempered

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the ordeal word

parts.note: a test is a trial or ordeal
ouch is what one says when hurt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in pain during an ordeal and is very grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy means irritable and easily offended; the superlative is most bad-tempered.

clue.text: Slow movement of a retreating old island tribe

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: An ancient island people are withdrawing slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow movement in a piece of music.

clue.text: You and I in style, moving in a gracious manner

indicators.note: in means the pronoun goes inside the rearranged letters
moving means shifting about, so the letters of style are rearranged

parts.note: we means you and I together

explanation.surface: Two people move elegantly together, in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the letters to SETLY; 'in' puts the pronoun inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetly means pleasantly and kindly, a synonym for graciously.
